# CS-08 — One-page charter under pressure

!!! info "Case card"
    **Difficulty:** Beginner (CS-01..CS-20) ·
    **Level:** L2 — Two-concept applied ·
    **Domain:** D2 · **Seed project:** CAMPUSHUB

## Learning objectives

1. Draft a charter that separates knowns, unknowns, and inventions.
2. Write objectives that are testable rather than aspirational.

## Project context

The Dean gives a rambling 10-minute brief: students complain, the old portal is 'a disaster', there is some money left this fiscal year, and the alumni office wants in. You have 40 minutes of class time to produce a one-page charter.

## Problem statement

Turn the messy brief into a charter with a testable objective, named sponsor, in/out scope, and explicit constraints.

## Constraints and available information

- One page maximum.
- Objective must be SMART and verifiable.
- Anything the brief did not specify becomes an open question, not an invention.

## Student tasks

1. Draft the charter (objective, scope in/out, sponsor, constraints, success criteria, top risk).
2. List the three questions you would put to the sponsor before sign-off.
3. Mark one item you deliberately left vague and why.

## Expected deliverables

- One-page charter.
- Three sponsor questions.

## Discussion questions

1. Which charter element is most often fake in student projects? Why?
1. Is it better to ship a charter with unknowns marked, or wait for answers?

## How you will be graded

Objective is genuinely testable (40%); scope in/out is explicit (30%); open questions separated from inventions (30%).

- Anchored in [Lecture 06](../lectures/L06-06-charter.md).
- Suggested use: in-class.
